en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on Offenses Entailing Expiation (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
Sappāṇaka-vagga 62.
The Training Rule on Living Beings.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks knowingly consumed water containing living beings.
Those monks who were of few desires... [and so on]... complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
"How can the group-of-six monks knowingly consume water containing living beings?"... [and so on]...
“Is it true, monks, that you knowingly consume water containing living beings?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... [as before]...
"How indeed, you foolish men, can you knowingly consume water containing living beings?
This, foolish men, does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And furthermore, monks, you should recite this training rule as follows:"
“Whatever monk, knowing that water contains living beings, should consume it, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Whatever monk” means whoever of such a kind... [as previously defined].
"Bhikkhu" ...
[as before] ... this is the "bhikkhu" intended in this context.
"Knows" means:
He knows it himself, or others inform him of it.
If he knows it contains living beings, or knowing that they will die by its use, he consumes it, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If it contains living beings and he perceives it as containing living beings, and he consumes it, there is an offense of expiation.
If he consumes [food] containing living beings while being in doubt [about it], there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If he consumes [food] containing living beings while perceiving it as being without living beings, there is no offense.
If he consumes [food] without living beings while perceiving it as containing living beings, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is waterless and he is in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If it is waterless and he perceives it as waterless, there is no offense.
There is no offense—
If one uses [the water] while not knowing it contains living beings, knowing it is free of living beings,
and knowing that [the recipient] will not die from its consumption, [there is no offense].
[It is] for one who is insane,
for a first-time offender.
The training rule on [water] containing living beings, the second, is finished.
